Nettle
NET-ul
noun
From the Old English netele; a stinging weed that springs up in waste and neglected ground, an emblem of desolation and judgment.

📖 Biblical Definition

The nettle is a coarse, stinging weed that springs up in waste places, ruined fields, and neglected ground, and so became in Scripture a steady emblem of desolation, slothfulness, and the judgment of God. The wise man, passing the field of the slothful and the vineyard of the man void of understanding, saw that “it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down” (Pro 24:31), and he took instruction from the sight against idleness. The prophets make the nettle the very mark of a land laid waste under the wrath of God. Zephaniah foretells of Moab and Ammon that they shall be “the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation” (Zep 2:9). Hosea warns rebellious Israel that “the pleasant places for their silver, nettles shall possess them: thorns shall be in their tabernacles” (Hos 9:6). And Job, in his abasement, describes the basest of men, driven out from among the living, who “among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together” (Job 30:7). Wherever the nettle spreads, the hand of man has failed and the curse has come in: the wall broken, the field forsaken, the dwelling emptied. The nettle preaches the bitter fruit of sloth and the desolation that follows the judgment of God, that what was once pleasant and fruitful becomes a thicket of stinging weeds.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A stinging weed of waste and neglected ground; emblem of the slothful’s ruin and of the desolation that follows the judgment of God.

expand to see more

NETTLE, a stinging weed that grows in waste ground.

It covered the field of the slothful (Pro 24:31).

Moab and Ammon become a breeding of nettles (Zep 2:9).

Nettles possess the pleasant places of judged Israel (Hos 9:6).

The basest of men gather under the nettles (Job 30:7).

📖 Key Scripture

Pro 24:31 — "And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down."

Zep 2:9 — "Therefore as I live, saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them."

Hos 9:6 — "For, lo, they are gone because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them up, Memphis shall bury them: the pleasant places for their silver, nettles shall possess them: thorns shall be in their tabernacles."

Job 30:7 — "Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

An agrarian image of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses the bitter fruit of sloth and the desolation that follows the judgment of God.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the desolation that sloth and sin bring upon a land. The wise man looked upon the field of the slothful and saw it grown over with thorns and covered with nettles, the wall broken down; and he received instruction against idleness. The nettle preaches that what is neglected does not stay empty but is overrun with stinging weeds, and that the ruin of the careless is the certain harvest of their sloth.

More solemnly, the prophets make the nettle the mark of a land laid waste under the judgment of God. Where the wrath of God has come in, the pleasant places are possessed by nettles, and the dwellings filled with thorns; Moab and Ammon become a breeding of nettles and a perpetual desolation. The weed that springs in ruined ground thus preaches the bitter end of rebellion against the LORD, when the fruitful field He gave is turned to a thicket of desolation.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Old English netele; a stinging weed of waste ground, emblem of sloth and judgment.

Nettle — from Old English netele.

A coarse, stinging weed of waste and neglected ground.

It covered the field of the slothful (Pro 24:31).

It marks lands laid waste under judgment (Zep 2:9; Hos 9:6).

The basest of men gather under it in their abasement (Job 30:7).

Usage

"Like the nettle over the slothful’s field, what is neglected is overrun with stinging weeds."

"The nettle teaches that ruin is the certain harvest of idleness and careless ground."

"Where the prophets see nettles spread, the judgment of God has turned the pleasant place to desolation."
